stories.headline: A Second Duck Has Appeared on the Jeep: Orange, Upright, and Facing the Direction of Keeps Ridge
body: At approximately half past seven this morning, Steve discovered a second rubber duck affixed to the Jeep's passenger-side mirror. It is orange. It is not the original duck, which remains on the driver's side facing north-northeast, as it has since Saturday. The new duck faces southeast — which is, Steve has noted in the margin of his current chart, the precise bearing of Keeps Ridge from the front drive.

The original duck has not moved. The two ducks now occupy opposite mirrors, facing each other at an angle of approximately forty-seven degrees, like two parties who have agreed to meet but have not yet been introduced. Steve described the arrangement as 'deliberate.' Christine described it as 'undeniably deliberate.' These are not the same word, and the distinction has been discussed.
No tracks. No note. The Duck Bandit has returned.

stories.headline: Tuesday Proceeds at Pace; Two Legacy Accounts Untangled Before Elevenses; Griphook the Younger Takes Notes Without Being Asked
body: Sources within Gringotts confirm that Tuesday opened briskly, with Christine resolving two legacy accounts whose paperwork had been circling in administrative limbo since the third goblin reorganisation of 1994. The accounts are now liquid, properly indexed, and — in one case — no longer technically haunted.

Most remarkably, Griphook the Younger was observed taking written notes during the eleven o'clock briefing, unprompted. Senior staff who witnessed the event have been asked to sign statutory declarations confirming what they saw. The document will be filed, framed, and kept behind glass.

stories.headline: Subcommittee Reconvenes on Forty Minutes' Notice; Describes New Duck as 'an Active Development'; Requests Permission to Feel Excited
body: The Ministry's Duck Affairs Subcommittee, which adjourned indefinitely last Sunday following the arc's resolution, was recalled to emergency session this afternoon after receiving Steve's field report on the orange duck. The chair described the development as 'an active and material development,' a phrase she had clearly been saving.

The subcommittee has formally requested permission from its parent committee to feel excited. The parent committee has not yet responded. In the meantime, subcommittee members have been asked to maintain procedural composure. This is going moderately well for some of them.

stories.headline: Dogs File Independent Assessments of the Orange Duck; Conclusions Differ
body: Lucy inspected the new duck from the driveway at a distance of approximately four feet. She then looked at Steve. Then back at the duck. She has filed no formal report, but her expression was described by one witness as 'professionally interested.'
Ellie approached the Jeep, noticed both ducks, and spent a meaningful moment greeting her own reflection in the bumper before returning inside. Her assessment of the ducks, if any, was not recorded.
Jersey remained on the sofa and submitted his views in absentia: the duck is fine, the sofa is warmer, and he is available for comment between two and four if someone brings him there.

familiars_corner: Lucy: Conducted a perimeter assessment of the Jeep at seven thirty-four. The orange duck was noted, catalogued, and cross-referenced against her private files. She has no comment at this time, which is itself a comment.
Ellie: Greeted her bumper reflection warmly, found it receptive, and considers the morning a social success. She also noticed something orange but assumed it was happy.
Jersey: Has requested that any further duck developments be summarised for him in writing and placed on the sofa cushion to his left, where he will review them at his convenience.
founding_editor_note: Two mirrors, two ducks, forty-seven degrees — whoever built that setup knew what they were doing. I'd have used a level, but the instinct is sound. — D.

in_brief.sport: The flint from Keeps Ridge has been formally weighed; it is heavier than it looks, which the household considers appropriate.
in_brief.forecast: Clear skies through Wednesday, with a forty percent chance of a third duck by the weekend; the subcommittee has already drafted contingency paperwork.

storyline_updates.title: The Duck Waits
storyline_updates.summary: Day 1: A second duck — orange, upright — has appeared on the Jeep's passenger-side mirror, facing southeast, which is the precise bearing of Keeps Ridge from the front drive. The original duck remains on the driver's side facing north-northeast. The two ducks now face each other at forty-seven degrees across the bonnet. No tracks, no note. The Ministry subcommittee has reconvened. Lucy has taken a professional interest. Day 2 should deepen the mystery: perhaps a detail about the orange duck itself (a marking, a number, a small imperfection) that suggests the Bandit knows something specific, or a second sighting — the Bandit seen at the edge of the drive, or another token left nearby. The forty-seven degree angle between ducks may prove significant.
